changes.before: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space. An inertial frame of the model is a tuple (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) consisting of an event o in A and an ordered basis (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) of V that is eta-orthonormal (eta(e_a,e_b) = diag(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}), future (e_0 is in C^+) and positively oriented (the ordered basis class of (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) is the fixed orientation of V). Its inertial chart is the map x: A -> R^4, x(p) := E^{-1}(p-o), where E: R^4 -> V is the linear isomorphism E(u) := sum_a u^a e_a; its components x^a(p) are the inertial coordinates of the event p, and x(p) = 0 exactly at p = o. The family of all inertial frames and charts is the inertial atlas of the model; two inertial charts x, x' are related by x' = M^{-1}(x - x(o')) for M the change-of-basis matrix between the two ordered bases, so transitions are affine bijections of R^4.
changes.after:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), with orientation fixed as a positive ray of
the determinant line $\Lambda^4V$
([[def-determinant-line-orientation-of-a-finite-dimensional-real-vector-space]])
and with the corresponding class of positively oriented ordered bases of $V$
([[def-orientation-of-a-finite-dimensional-real-vector-space]]); by
[[prop-orientations-and-positive-basis-classes-agree-in-positive-dimension]] the
positive ray selects exactly one such class for $\dim V=4>0$.

An **inertial frame** of the model is a tuple $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ consisting
of an event $o\in A$ and an ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $V$ that is

1. **$\eta$-orthonormal**: $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ for all $a,b$ ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]]);
2. **future**: $e_0\in C^+$, i.e. $e_0$ is future timelike; and
3. **positively oriented**: the ordered basis lies in the positive-basis class
   selected by the fixed orientation.

The event $o$ is the **origin** of the frame and $e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ are its
**basis vectors**.

**Inertial charts.** For an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, define

$$E:\mathbb R^4\longrightarrow V,\qquad E(u):=\sum_{a=0}^3u^ae_a .$$

Then $E$ is a linear isomorphism ([[def-linear-isomorphism-and-invertible-linear-map]]):
it is linear by construction, and it is bijective because
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is an ordered basis, every $v\in V$ having exactly one
coordinate list $u$ with $v=\sum_au^ae_a$
([[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]). The **inertial
chart** of the frame is the map

$$x:A\longrightarrow\mathbb R^4,\qquad x(p):=E^{-1}(p-o),$$

and its values $x^a(p)$ are the **inertial coordinates of the event $p$** in the
frame. Since $E$ and $v\mapsto p+v$ are bijections, $x$ is a bijection
$A\to\mathbb R^4$; and $x(p)=0$ exactly when $p-o=0_V$, that is, exactly when
$p=o$.

**Transition law.** Let $(o';e'_0,e'_1,e'_2,e'_3)$ be another inertial frame
with chart $x'$, and let $M=(M^b_a)$ be the change-of-basis matrix defined by
$e'_a=\sum_bM^b_ae_b$, a $4\times4$ real matrix that is invertible because both
families are ordered bases. Then $E'(u)=\sum_au^ae'_a=E(Mu)$ for all
$u\in\mathbb R^4$, for the matrix-vector product $Mu$ in the coordinates of the
first frame, because $\sum_au^a\sum_bM^b_ae_b=\sum_b(\sum_aM^b_au^a)e_b$; hence
$E'=E\circ M$ and $E'^{-1}=M^{-1}\circ E^{-1}$, so for every event $p$,

$$x'(p)=M^{-1}\bigl(x(p)-x(o')\bigr)=M^{-1}x(p)-M^{-1}x(o') .$$

In particular the transition between two inertial charts is an affine map of
$\mathbb R^4$ with invertible linear part $M^{-1}$ and constant part
$-M^{-1}x(o')$, and it is a bijection of $\mathbb R^4$ with inverse
$u\mapsto Mu+x(o')$, which is the transition in the reverse direction.

**The inertial atlas.** The **inertial atlas** of the model is the family of
all inertial frames together with their inertial charts. Its charts are
available at every event by [[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]], which
supplies for every $o\in A$ an inertial frame with origin $o$; and any two of
its charts are related by the affine transition displayed above.

changes.before: For $z\in[-1,1]$ define the real polynomial $P_l(z)=\pi^{-1}\int_0^\pi\bigl[z+i\sqrt{1-z^2}\,\cos\theta\bigr]^l\,d\theta$, $l\in\mathbb N_0$. Then $P_l$ is a real polynomial of degree at most $l$ with $|P_l(z)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$, $P_l(1)=1$, and for $|q|<1$ the series $\sum_{l\ge0}q^lP_l(z)$ converges absolutely and uniformly on $[-1,1]$ with $$(1-2qz+q^2)^{-1/2}=\sum_{l=0}^{\infty}q^lP_l(z),$$ where the branch is the analytic square root equal to $1$ at $q=0$ ([[def-series-of-real-functions]], [[thm-weierstrass-m-test-for-function-series]]). Consequently, for $r>|y|$ with $n=x/|x|$ and $N\in\mathbb N_0$, $\bigl|\,|x-y|^{-1}-\sum_{l=0}^{N}|y|^l|x|^{-l-1}P_l(n\cdot y/|y|)\bigr|\le|y|^{N+1}|x|^{-N-2}(1-|y|/|x|)^{-1}$, uniformly on $|y|\le a<r$ (with $y=0$ interpreted by the zero higher terms), and after integrating against an $L^1$ source the corresponding multipole expansion converges with that error times its $L^1$ norm. For the integrated $L^1$-source and every-spatial-derivative assertions, assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) through the Lebesgue and harmonic-estimate interfaces. On an observation compact set disjoint from $\overline{B_a(0)}$ every fixed spatial derivative series converges uniformly, uniformly also over $|y|\le a$, by harmonicity of the coefficient terms and [[thm-interior-derivative-estimates-for-harmonic-functions]]. The initial finite-Riemann polynomial/generating assertions are choice-free. This lemma supplies the convergent zonal kernel; it does not by itself prove a spherical $L^2$ basis or boundary convergence.

changes.before: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. For $k>0$ define $G_k(x)=e^{ik|x|}/(4\pi|x|)$ off the origin, a locally integrable complex function. Then $$(-\Delta-k^2)G_k=\delta_0$$ distributionally. For a finite complex measure $\alpha$ supported in $B_a(0)$, the field $u=G_k*\alpha$ is smooth outside the support, solves $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ there and is outgoing: for $x=rn$, $r\ge2a$, $$u(rn)=\frac{e^{ikr}}{4\pi r}\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}\,d\alpha(y)+O\!\Bigl(\frac{\|\alpha\|_{\mathrm{TV}}}{r}\Bigl[\frac{a}{r}+\frac{ka^2}{r}\Bigr]\Bigr)$$ uniformly in direction, and $r(\partial_ru-iku)=O(r^{-1})$ uniformly. For a planar aperture $y=(y_1,y_2,0)$ with observation $x=(\xi_1,\xi_2,z)$, $z>0$, $|\xi|\le b$, $a+b\ll z$, the Fresnel approximation replaces $R=|x-y|$ by $z+|\xi-y|^2/(2z)$ and $1/R$ by $1/z$ with phase error $O(k(a+b)^4/z^3)$ and relative amplitude error $O((a+b)^2/z^2)$, hence absolute field error $O(\|\alpha\|_{\mathrm{TV}}z^{-1}[(a+b)^2/z^2+k(a+b)^4/z^3])$. Aperture data are an explicitly specified scalar source, not asserted to be the unknown exact Maxwell boundary traces, and no uniqueness or existence for arbitrary obstacle boundary data is claimed.

changes.before: Let $c>0$, let $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ (unbounded $f$ is allowed), and define the spherical mean $$M_rf(x)=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}f(x+rn)\,d\Omega(n),\qquad r\ge0,$$ with the outward sphere measure of total area $4\pi$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]). Then $r\mapsto M_rf(x)$ is smooth for $r\ge0$ and satisfies the Euler-Poisson-Darboux identity $$\partial_r^2M_rf(x)+\frac2r\partial_rM_rf(x)=\Delta M_rf(x)\qquad(r>0),$$ and the function $H_f(x,t)=t\,M_{ct}f(x)$, $t\ge0$, satisfies $$\partial_t^2H_f=c^2\Delta H_f,\qquad H_f(x,0)=0,\qquad \partial_tH_f(x,0)=f(x).$$ All identities are local and need no decay of $f$, since every integration set is compact. changes.before:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the explicitly used variational, Sobolev and compact-spectral suppliers. Let the PEC classes be those of [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]: for a bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$, $X$ is the graph-norm closure in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the smooth fields on the closure with $n\times u=0$, $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$ and $H=\overline V^{\,L^2}$. Then:
(a) **Smooth cavity.** The curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis $\{u_j\}$ with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity, $\lambda_j\to\infty$ whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, and a finite-dimensional zero eigenspace that is retained; the eigen-equation $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ holds distributionally with the PEC trace. For every chosen positive mathematical speed $v_{\mathrm{wave}}>0$ and every displacement datum $q_0\in V$ and velocity datum $q_1\in H$, the associated second-order wave has coefficients $a_j''+v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_ja_j=0$. Displacement lies in $C(\mathbb R;V)$, velocity in $C(\mathbb R;H)$, and finite modal sums converge in these respective norms uniformly on compact time intervals. The finitely many $\lambda=0$ modes remain $a_j(t)=a_j(0)+ta_j'(0)$. The speed is a positive abstract parameter and has no physical dependency. The eigenfields are $C^\infty$ on the closure by [[lem-em-pec-cavity-eigenfield-boundary-regularity]], applied to the full-$X$ eigenvariational identity of the cavity supplier. The shifted scalar auxiliary boundary problems are solvable on the declared bounded smooth domain by [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]]; the specific scalar Dirichlet resolvent and its smooth-zero-boundary test density used in G3 are supplied by its recorded local resolvent lemma.
(b) **Rectangular class.** For every rectangular box $Q=\prod_j(0,L_j)$ with $L_j>0$ and every pair of positive mathematical coefficients $\varepsilon,\mu>0$, the separable products described in the mode verification are dense in the reflection-parity energy class, and every initial datum of that class has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the class with constant energy, with finite separated modes dense at every time. The rectangular statements are the recorded rectangular reflection-class completeness lemma [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] (the $G2$ branch); the individual TE/TM mode verification against the Maxwell equations and the PEC conditions is the recorded $G1$ physics branch, homed on the physical guide page and not consumed here as a mathematical premise. No completeness in lossy, open-ended or non-smooth classes is asserted.
changes.after:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain in the local graph sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], with outward Euclidean unit normal field $\nu$ on $\partial\Omega$. Restate the class conventions of [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]: $L^2:=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ is the real Hilbert space of square integrable vector fields with the inner product $\langle u,v\rangle=\int_\Omega u\cdot v\,dx$ induced by the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and
$$H(\operatorname{curl})=\{u\in L^2:\operatorname{curl}u\in L^2\},\qquad H(\operatorname{div})=\{u\in L^2:\operatorname{div}u\in L^2\}$$
are the graph spaces with norms $\|u\|^2_{H(\operatorname{curl})}=\|u\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{curl}u\|_2^2$ and $\|u\|^2_{H(\operatorname{div})}=\|u\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}u\|_2^2$, the curl and divergence being taken in the distributional sense; $X$ is the graph-norm closure in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the fields that are smooth on a neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$ and satisfy $\nu\times u=0$ pointwise on $\partial\Omega$; and $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$, $H=\overline V^{\,L^2}$. This is the explicit weak perfect-electric-conductor class of that item, not an identification with every maximal tangential-trace realisation.

Then:

(a) **Smooth PEC cavity.** The curl form $(u,v)\mapsto\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u\cdot\operatorname{curl}v$ on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis $\{u_j\}$ with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity, with $\lambda_j\to\infty$ whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional and with the finite-dimensional zero eigenspace retained. Each eigenfield $u_j\in V$ satisfies $\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u_j\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=\lambda_j\int_\Omega u_j\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$; the eigen-equation $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ holds distributionally together with the PEC trace; and $u_j$ has a $C^\infty$ representative on $\overline\Omega$ for which $\operatorname{div}u_j=0$, $\nu\times u_j=0$ and $\partial_\nu u_{j,n}+(\operatorname{div}\nu)u_{j,n}=0$ hold classically on $\partial\Omega$, where $u_{j,n}=u_j\cdot\nu$ and $\nu$ is extended constant along collar normal lines. For every explicitly chosen positive mathematical speed $v_{\mathrm{wave}}>0$ and every pair of data $q_0\in V$, $q_1\in H$, the associated second-order wave has coefficients solving $a_j''+v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_ja_j=0$ with $a_j(0)=\langle q_0,u_j\rangle$ and $a_j'(0)=\langle q_1,u_j\rangle$, in the modal class of that item: its displacement lies in $C(\mathbb R;V)$ and its velocity in $C(\mathbb R;H)$, finite modal sums converge in $C(K;V)$ and $C(K;H)$ on every compact time interval $K$, and the finitely many $\lambda_j=0$ modes are $a_j(t)=a_j(0)+ta_j'(0)$. The speed is a positive abstract mathematical parameter and has no physical dependency. The scalar auxiliary Dirichlet resolvent used inside the recorded cavity argument has, for every $q\in L^2(\Omega)$, a unique solution $\varphi\in H_0^1(\Omega)\cap H^2(\Omega)$ of $(1-\Delta)\varphi=q$, with smooth zero-boundary approximants converging in $H^2$ and whose gradients converge in the PEC graph norm, by [[lem-em-dirichlet-resolvent-h-two-and-smooth-test-density]]. For smooth $q$ this solution is smooth on the closure by the same smooth-boundary bootstrap; no classical regularity for a general $L^2$ datum is asserted. Smooth unshifted scalar boundary problems have the classical upgrade of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] with $\varepsilon=I$.

(b) **Rectangular reflection-parity class.** Let $Q=\prod_{j=1}^3(0,L_j)$ with $L_j>0$ and let $\varepsilon,\mu>0$ be constants. In the reflection boundary class of [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] (real $L^2$ fields on the torus $\prod_j\mathbb R/(2L_j\mathbb Z)$ whose components carry the parities of that item and whose distributional divergences vanish), the finite separated Fourier modes are dense at every time, and every initial datum of the class has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the class, along which $\tfrac12\int_Q(\varepsilon|E|^2+|B|^2/\mu)\,dx$ is constant.

No completeness is asserted in lossy, open-ended or non-smooth classes, and the constant-Ohmic and open-longitudinal branches are homed separately as physical items on the guide page; they are not mathematical premises or dependencies of this statement.

changes.before: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space, let x and x' be inertial charts whose transition is the affine map x'(p) = Lambda x(p) + b with linear part Lambda (a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix by lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz), and let Omega be an open subset of A. Let J: Omega -> V, k, and T be a C^k vector field, a C^k covector field and a C^k type-(r,s) tensor field on Omega in the sense of def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space, with components J^a, k_a and T^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s} in the chart x, and primed components in the chart x'. Then: (i) J'^a = Lambda^a_b J^b: a contravariant index gains the factor Lambda^a_b, i.e. components transform by multiplication with the transition matrix. (ii) k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b: a covariant index gains the factor (Lambda^{-1})^b_a. If theta(p) = k_a x^a(p) + theta_0 is an affine scalar function with constant covector k and constant theta_0, then theta(p) = k'_a x'^a(p) + theta'_0 with k' as above and theta'_0 := theta_0 - k'_a b^a, so the phase function is invariant when the constant term is transformed together with the covector. (iii) T'^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s} = Lambda^{a_1}_{c_1} ... Lambda^{a_r}_{c_r} (Lambda^{-1})^{d_1}_{b_1} ... (Lambda^{-1})^{d_s}_{b_s} T^{c_1...c_r}_{d_1...d_s}: every contravariant index gains a factor Lambda and every covariant index a factor Lambda^{-1}, and the law is consistent with the multilinear evaluation of T(p) after substituting the transformed basis. Every contraction of one contravariant with one covariant index is invariant, and the metric components satisfy eta'_{ab} = eta_{ab}. (iv) The coordinate partial derivatives satisfy partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b wherever the derivatives exist. Consequently the divergence of a vector field is invariant, partial'_a J'^a = partial_a J^a, and for a C^1 type-(2,0) field T one has partial'_a T'^{ab} = Lambda^b_c partial_a T^{ac}. (v) Alternating covariant tensor fields transform by the covariant law on each slot; the oriented volume form of the model satisfies epsilon'_{abcd} = epsilon_{abcd}, since det Lambda = +1, whereas a general Lorentz matrix with det = -1 changes its sign. (vi) Let J be a C^1 vector field with components (J^0,J^1,J^2,J^3) in an inertial chart, and write the spatial block as J_cov := (J^1,J^2,J^3) and denote by partial_i the spatial partial derivatives in the chart. Then the continuity equation partial_a J^a = 0 is equivalent to partial_0 J^0 + sum_i partial_i J^i = 0, and under the passive boost with parameter beta (Lambda = B(beta), Lambda^{-1} = B(-beta)) the components transform as J'^0 = gamma(J^0 - beta . J_cov), J'_cov = J_cov + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . J_cov) beta - gamma beta J^0. (vii) If U is a C^1 future timelike vector field and rho_0 a C^1 scalar field, then J:=rho_0 U is a C^1 vector field and its first component is J^0=rho_0 U^0. Future timelikeness gives U^0>0 in every inertial chart, so define the normalized chart direction u:=U/U^0 and the coordinate density rho:=J^0. Then u^0=1, u^i=U^i/U^0, rho=rho_0 U^0, and J=rho u pointwise. The coordinate density rho and scalar multiplier rho_0 are different objects: rho=rho_0 if and only if rho_0(U^0−1)=0; at points where rho_0!=0 equality holds exactly when U^0=1. The vector u is a normalized chart direction; it is not assumed to have unit or four-velocity normalization. In an x^0=ct convention the associated spatial coordinate velocity, if interpreted as such, has components c u^i; physical current/density identification requires its own model premise. Interpretation boundary: the identification of a physical charge-current with a vector field, and of rho with a measured charge density, is a model premise of the electromagnetic framework; this item is a statement about the transformation of components of specified fields and does not by itself assert that any physical current transforms as a vector.

inertial charts whose transition is the affine map $x'(p)=\Lambda x(p)+b$ with

$\mathcal C^k$ vector field, a $\mathcal C^k$ covector field and a
$\mathcal C^k$ type-$(r,s)$ tensor field on $\Omega$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], with components $J^a$, $k_a$ and
$T^{a_1\dots a_r}{}_{b_1\dots b_s}$ in the chart $x$, and primed components in
the chart $x'$. Then:

(i) $J'^a=\Lambda^a{}_bJ^b$: a contravariant index gains the factor
$\Lambda^a{}_b$, that is, components transform by multiplication with the
transition matrix;

(ii) $k'_a=(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_ak_b$: a covariant index gains the factor
$(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_a$. If $\theta(p)=k_ax^a(p)+\theta_0$ is an affine scalar
function with constant covector $k$ and constant $\theta_0$, then
$\theta(p)=k'_ax'^a(p)+\theta'_0$ with $k'$ as above and
$\theta'_0:=\theta_0-k'_ab^a$, so the phase function is invariant when the
constant term is transformed together with the covector;

(iii) $T'^{a_1\dots a_r}{}_{b_1\dots b_s}
=\Lambda^{a_1}{}_{c_1}\cdots\Lambda^{a_r}{}_{c_r}
(\Lambda^{-1})^{d_1}{}_{b_1}\cdots(\Lambda^{-1})^{d_s}{}_{b_s}
T^{c_1\dots c_r}{}_{d_1\dots d_s}$: every contravariant index gains a factor
$\Lambda$ and every covariant index a factor $\Lambda^{-1}$, and the law is
consistent with the multilinear evaluation of $T(p)$ after substituting the
transformed basis. Every contraction of one contravariant with one covariant
index is invariant, and the metric components satisfy
$\eta'_{ab}=\eta_{ab}$;

(iv) the coordinate partial-derivative operators satisfy
$\partial'_a=(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_a\partial_b$ when applied to scalar functions
at points where their coordinate representations are totally differentiable.
Consequently, at every event where the component functions of $J$ are totally
differentiable, the divergence is invariant,
$\partial'_aJ'^a=\partial_aJ^a$. These total differentials exist at every
event if $k\ge1$; for $k=0$ this clause applies only at events where the
specified components are totally differentiable, and does not assert
covariance from the existence of separate partial derivatives alone. For a
$\mathcal C^1$ type-$(2,0)$ field $T$ one has
$\partial'_aT'^{ab}=\Lambda^b{}_c\partial_aT^{ac}$;

(v) alternating covariant tensor fields transform by the covariant law on each
slot; the oriented volume form of the model satisfies
$\epsilon'_{abcd}=\epsilon_{abcd}$, since $\det\Lambda=+1$, whereas a general
Lorentz matrix with $\det=-1$ changes its sign;

(vi) let $J$ be a $\mathcal C^1$ vector field with components
$(J^0,J^1,J^2,J^3)$ in an inertial chart, and write the spatial block as
$J_{\mathrm{cov}}:=(J^1,J^2,J^3)$ and denote by $\partial_i$ the spatial
partial derivatives in the chart. Then the continuity equation
$\partial_aJ^a=0$ is equivalent to
$\partial_0J^0+\sum_i\partial_iJ^i=0$, and under the passive boost with
parameter $\boldsymbol\beta$ ($\Lambda=B(\boldsymbol\beta)$,
$\Lambda^{-1}=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)$) the components transform as
$J'^0=\gamma(J^0-\boldsymbol\beta\cdot J_{\mathrm{cov}})$ and
$J'_{\mathrm{cov}}=J_{\mathrm{cov}}
+\frac{\gamma-1}{|\boldsymbol\beta|^2}(\boldsymbol\beta\cdot J_{\mathrm{cov}})\boldsymbol\beta
-\gamma\boldsymbol\beta J^0$;

(vii) if $U$ is a $\mathcal C^1$ future timelike vector field and $\rho_0$ a
$\mathcal C^1$ scalar field, then $J:=\rho_0U$ is a $\mathcal C^1$ vector field
and its first component is $J^0=\rho_0U^0$. Future timelikeness gives $U^0>0$
in every inertial chart, so one may define the normalized chart direction
$u:=U/U^0$ and the coordinate density $\rho:=J^0$. Then $u^0=1$,
$u^i=U^i/U^0$, $\rho=\rho_0U^0$, and $J=\rho u$ pointwise. The coordinate
density $\rho$ and scalar multiplier $\rho_0$ are different objects:
$\rho=\rho_0$ if and only if $\rho_0(U^0-1)=0$; at points where
$\rho_0\neq0$ equality holds exactly when $U^0=1$. The vector $u$ is a
normalized chart direction; it is not assumed to have unit or four-velocity
normalization. In an $x^0=ct$ convention the associated spatial coordinate
velocity, if interpreted as such, has components $cu^i$; physical
current/density identification requires its own model premise.

**Interpretation boundary.** The identification of a physical charge-current
with a vector field, and of $\rho$ with a measured charge density, is a model
premise of the electromagnetic framework; this item is a statement about the
transformation of components of specified fields and does not by itself assert
that any physical current transforms as a vector.

Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its frame basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, its SI units and its fields $E,B$ be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]] and [[def-em-fields]]. Fix $a,b>0$, write $x_t=(x_1,x_2)$, $e_z:=e_3$, and define $\nabla_t f=(\partial_1f,\partial_2f,0)$, $\Delta_t f=\partial_1^2f+\partial_2^2f$ and $\operatorname{div}_tu_t=\partial_1u_1+\partial_2u_2$ for the stated regularity, using [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]].
(a) [Straight guide] A straight guide region is $\Omega_A:=A\times\mathbb R$ where $A$ is either a bounded connected $C^1$ plane domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]) or the explicit rectangular cross-section; the rectangle has corners and is treated by its open faces, not asserted to be a $C^1$ boundary domain, with longitudinal axis $e_z$; for a rectangular cross-section $A=R_{ab}:=(0,a)\times(0,b)$ the region is called the rectangular guide and its walls are the four open faces $\{x_1=0\},\{x_1=a\},\{x_2=0\},\{x_2=b\}$. A rectangular cavity region is $\Omega_c:=(0,a)\times(0,b)\times(0,d)$ for fixed $d>0$, with the six open faces as its walls. The separate smooth-cavity spectral branch uses an explicitly declared bounded $C^\infty$ domain in $\mathbb R^3$ with its smooth PEC boundary; it is not the rectangular reflection class. Spatial derivatives are taken at fixed $t$; the fields are defined on $\Omega\times I$ with the regularity declared by each theorem.
(b) [PEC boundary model] On every open wall (a wall minus its edges) the ideal perfectly conducting boundary model declares the two conditions $n\times E=0$ and $n\cdot B=0$, where $n$ is the outward unit normal of that wall ($-e_1,+e_1,-e_2,+e_2$ on the four rectangular walls, and $\pm e_j$ on the six cavity walls). Its physical reading is the ideal-conductor limit of the stationary interface conditions of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]]: with $E=B=0$ inside the ideal conductor the tangential electric field and the normal magnetic field vanish, while the surface-charge and surface-current readings $n\cdot D=\sigma_f$ and $n\times H=K_f$ are determined by the traces and are not prescribed here. The supplier's hypotheses (a compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with one-sided $C^1$ fields) cover a smooth stationary interface, not the $\sigma\to\infty$ idealization nor the box edges; the guide/cavity conditions on the open walls are therefore declared as an idealization of this definition, and no pointwise statement on the edges is made.
(c) [Zero-normal-B reflection class] For the rectangular box $Q=\prod_{j=1}^3(0,L_j)$ with $L=(a,b,d)$, the reflection class is the class of locally integrable fields $E,B$ on $Q$ whose extensions to the rectangular torus $\prod_j\mathbb R/(2L_j\mathbb Z)$, defined by extending $E_1$ evenly across the $x_1$-walls and oddly across the $x_2$-, $x_3$-walls and cyclically for $E_2,E_3$, and extending $B_1$ oddly across $x_1$ and evenly across $x_2,x_3$ and cyclically for $B_2,B_3$, are $L^2$ fields, together with the distributional constraints that $\operatorname{div}E$ and $\operatorname{div}B$ vanish on the torus for the extensions. This is the declared weak PEC model used for the cavity initial-value problem; for smooth fields the parities give $n\times E=0$ and $n\cdot B=0$ on $\partial Q$. Initial data not in this class (for example data with trapped normal $B$) are excluded, as are the general $H(\operatorname{curl})$ boundary classes, which are defined by the mathematical suppliers and are not identified here with the classical conditions.
(d) [TE, TM, TEM] For a guide or cavity field $(E,B)$, the longitudinal components are $E_z:=E\cdot e_z$ and $B_z:=B\cdot e_z$; the field is called TE (transverse electric) if $E_z\equiv0$, TM (transverse magnetic) if $B_z\equiv0$, and TEM if both vanish, always relative to the named axis $e_z$.
(e) [Separated phasor convention] For $\omega>0$ and $\beta\in\mathbb C$, a $\beta$-$\omega$ separated phasor field on the guide is a real field of the form $F(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\tilde F(x_1,x_2)e^{i(\beta x_3-\omega t)}\bigr)$ with a complex amplitude $\tilde F$, componentwise; $\omega/(2\pi)$ is the frequency and $\beta$ the longitudinal propagation constant; when $\beta$ is real, $\beta>0$ describes propagation in the $+e_z$ direction under this phase convention, while a complex $\beta$ gives the spatial factor $e^{-\operatorname{Im}\beta x_3}$ and may grow in the opposite direction; each consuming branch states its selection.
(f) [Scope] The definition fixes the geometry, the PEC boundary model, the weak reflection class and the mode terminology; it asserts no field equation, no constitutive law and no existence or completeness of modes, Rectangular TE/TM candidates and the rectangular reflection class, declared smooth bounded PEC cavity spectral classes, and smooth straight-guide TEM potential branches (including the coaxial annulus) are within this geometry. No general non-rectangular TE/TM guide theory, circular-guide spectral classification, open-end or junction scattering, or arbitrary lossy model is supplied. The same stationary PEC geometry also hosts the explicitly declared constant scalar Ohmic cavity class and the full longitudinal finite-energy reflection class of the straight rectangular guide; constitutive and evolution claims belong to their consuming theorems, not this definition.

changes.before: Adopt the postulates post-sr-inertial-covariance, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and the causal signal restriction post-sr-causal-signal-propagation, and use the events, the relations <= and < and the sets J^+ and I^+ of def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space together with the mathematical results lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion, lem-sr-spacelike-pairs-have-frame-dependent-time-order and thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence. Let x be the chart of any inertial frame with x^0 = c t (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart, def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions). Then, as conditional statements about the ideal model and not about any actual apparatus: (i) Receipt in the future light cone and absolute temporal order. If a signal is transmitted from p to q, then q is in J^+(p); if q is not p, then x^0(q) > x^0(p) and |x_s(q) - x_s(p)| <= x^0(q) - x^0(p) in every inertial chart, and every inertial frame's time order places the reception after the emission. Hence no inertial change of description reports the reception before the emission, and the temporal order of the endpoints of a transmission is the same in every inertial frame. (ii) Relay composition. If signals are transmitted from p to q and from q to r, then r is in J^+(p); if in addition q is in I^+(p) or r is in I^+(q), then r is in I^+(p). Thus relaying never leaves the causal future of the first emission and never returns to the emission event. (iii) No closed signal loop. If signals are transmitted from p to q and from q to p, then p = q; no chain of transmissions in this model returns to its own emission event. (iv) Frame independence of signal reachability. For every proper orthochronous affine Lorentz map F of the model, which is an inertial change of description by post-sr-inertial-covariance, one has F(J^+(p)) = J^+(F(p)) and F(I^+(p)) = I^+(F(p)) for all events p, and p <= q if and only if F(p) <= F(q); hence whether the model admits a signal between two events is the same in every inertial frame, in agreement with pthm-sr-interval-and-cone-invariance. (v) Spacelike pairs admit no signal. If q - p is spacelike, then no signal is transmitted from p to q, while there are inertial frames whose charts assign x^0(q) - x^0(p) either sign; consequently the model's signal restriction is exactly the requirement that transmissions occur only between events whose temporal order is observer-independent. (vi) Scope and qualification. Every clause is conditional on the adopted postulates and is a statement about the ideal flat model; no actual signal, transmitter, receiver, detector or measurement is described, no statistical or empirical claim is made, and no inference from the model's structure to the physical world is drawn. Clause (v) uses the mathematical fact lem-sr-spacelike-pairs-have-frame-dependent-time-order and not an experiment. No choice principle is used.
changes.after:
Adopt the postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]],
[[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and the causal signal restriction
[[post-sr-causal-signal-propagation]], and use the events, the relations $\le$
and $<$ and the sets $J^+$ and $I^+$ of
[[def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space]] together with the
mathematical results
[[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]],
[[lem-sr-spacelike-pairs-have-frame-dependent-time-order]] and
[[thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence]]. Let $x$ be the chart of
any inertial frame with $x^0=ct$
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]],
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]). Then, as conditional
statements about the ideal model and not about any actual apparatus:

**(i) Receipt in the future light cone and absolute temporal order.** If a
signal is transmitted from $p$ to $q$, then $q\in J^+(p)$; if $q\ne p$, then
$x^0(q)>x^0(p)$ and $|x_s(q)-x_s(p)|\le x^0(q)-x^0(p)$ in every inertial chart,
and every inertial frame's time order places the reception after the emission.
Hence no inertial change of description reports the reception before the
emission, and the temporal order of the endpoints of a transmission is the same
in every inertial frame.

**(ii) Relay composition.** If signals are transmitted from $p$ to $q$ and from
$q$ to $r$, then $r\in J^+(p)$; if in addition $q\in I^+(p)$ or
$r\in I^+(q)$, then $r\in I^+(p)$. Thus relaying never leaves the causal future
of the first emission; a relay with at least one nonzero leg never returns to
the emission event.

**(iii) No closed signal loop.** If signals are transmitted from $p$ to $q$ and
from $q$ to $p$, then $p=q$. More generally, a finite chain of transmissions is closed if and
only if every leg has zero displacement; no nontrivial chain returns to its
own emission event.

**(iv) Frame independence of signal reachability.** For every proper
orthochronous affine Lorentz map $F$ of the model, which is an inertial change
of description by [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], one has
$F(J^+(p))=J^+(F(p))$ and $F(I^+(p))=I^+(F(p))$ for all events $p$, and
$p\le q$ if and only if $F(p)\le F(q)$; hence whether the model admits a signal
between two events is the same in every inertial frame, in agreement with
[[pthm-sr-interval-and-cone-invariance]].

**(v) Spacelike pairs admit no signal.** If $q-p$ is spacelike, then no signal
is transmitted from $p$ to $q$, while there are inertial frames whose charts
assign $x^0(q)-x^0(p)$ either sign; consequently the model's signal restriction
is exactly the requirement that transmissions occur only between events whose
temporal order is observer-independent, with the emission the earlier endpoint.

**(vi) Scope and qualification.** Every clause is conditional on the adopted
postulates and is a statement about the ideal flat model; no actual signal,
transmitter, receiver, detector or measurement is described, no statistical or
empirical claim is made, and no inference from the model's structure to the
physical world is drawn. Clause (v) uses the mathematical fact
[[lem-sr-spacelike-pairs-have-frame-dependent-time-order]] and not an
experiment. No choice principle is used.
